title: Mirabel and the Clock
premise: In the winter of 1899, field hospital nurse Noor Montrose secretly records the names of soldiers erased from official ledgers, a quiet act of rebellion in a garrison town ruled by Colonel Ashworth, whose career is built on convenient omissions. When a frightened girl named Mirabel is abandoned at the hospital door clutching a pocket watch that contains proof of Ashworth's falsified casualty reports, Noor must choose between safety and truth. Smuggling the watch and the child past three military checkpoints before the new century is proclaimed, Noor is betrayed by the colleague she trusted most, loses nearly everything, and ultimately delivers the evidence to a visiting inspector as midnight strikes. Ashworth falls, Mirabel finds a home with Noor, and the forgotten names are read aloud into the record.
about_author: Kestrel Fairweather is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing military hospital records from the late nineteenth century. Fascinated by the small hands that kept history honest, Fairweather writes fiction about the people official histories forgot.

chapters.title: The Ledger Under the Floorboard
chapters.summary: Noor Montrose, POV. Working the fever ward of a garrison hospital in the last weeks of 1899, Noor tends soldiers while privately recording the names officers strike from the rolls. We learn her brother was one such erased name. Emotional beat: quiet, disciplined grief channeled into secret defiance.

chapters.title: A Child at the Door
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. On a freezing night, a girl of about seven, Mirabel, is left at the hospital entrance with a pocket watch sewn into her coat and a note: forget the face. The watch's hidden compartment holds documents in a dead officer's hand. Emotional beat: dread and reluctant responsibility as Noor recognizes the handwriting of an erased name.

chapters.title: What the Watch Contained
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. Deciphering the documents with the help of clerk Tobias Fenwick, Noor learns they prove Colonel Ashworth falsified casualty reports to hide a massacre he ordered covered up. Ashworth begins hunting a missing ledger and a missing child. Emotional beat: the dawning weight of what she holds.

chapters.title: The Colonel's Courtesy
chapters.summary: Ashworth, POV. The colonel inspects the hospital with velvet menace, questioning Noor over tea while his men search the wards. He offers promotion for loyalty. Noor lies smoothly and hates how easily it comes. Emotional beat: the seductive, corrupting comfort of power measured against a nurse's steady nerve.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. Noor maps her escape: the hospital gate, the river bridge, the railway barrier, each guarded, each tightening as New Year's Eve approaches and an inspector from the War Office arrives. Tobias agrees to help, and Noor allows herself to trust him. Emotional beat: fragile hope and the first stirrings of loyalty beyond duty.

chapters.title: Mirabel's Version
chapters.summary: Mirabel, POV. In the child's voice: the soldier who carried her was her father, one of Ashworth's erased dead; the watch was his insurance. Mirabel's memories fill gaps in the documents. Emotional beat: innocence bearing witness, and Noor's resolve hardening from caution into conviction.

chapters.title: The Bridge at Dusk
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. First checkpoint: Noor smuggles Mirabel through the hospital gate in a laundry cart, then onto the crowded bridge where a sentry recognizes the coat. A stranger vouches for them at cost to himself. Emotional beat: terror, gratitude, and the discovery that quiet kindness is everywhere among the powerless.

chapters.title: The Turncoat
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. At the river checkpoint Tobias betrays them, trading Mirabel's whereabouts for his own pardon. Noor escapes with the watch but loses the girl to Ashworth's men. Emotional beat: devastation, and the theme made flesh—loyalty bought is loyalty sold.

chapters.title: Midnight Business
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. Climax. At the New Year's Eve assembly, Ashworth prepares to proclaim the century with his record intact and Mirabel held as leverage. Noor walks past the final checkpoint in plain sight, opens the watch before the War Office inspector as church bells strike twelve, and names the dead aloud. Emotional beat: courage at maximum cost, truth spoken in the belly of power.

chapters.title: The Names Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Noor, POV. Resolution. Ashworth is relieved of command and court-martialed; Tobias, pitiable rather than wicked, is dismissed. Noor's ledger is entered into the official record, each erased name restored. She takes Mirabel home. Emotional beat: hard-won peace—truth survived, and so, at last, did they.
